evidence.text: 后 (empress) and its mirror image 司 (take charge) were originally used interchangeably. The origin of both characters is unclear. In simplified Chinese 后 is also used to mean "after, behind", while in traditional Chinese this meaning is written with a separate character 後.
繼體君也。象人之形。施令以告四方，故厂之。从一、口。發號者，君后也。凡后之屬皆从后。

Oracle bone inscriptions often wrote 后 as 毓, depicting a woman giving birth. Wang Guowei posits the meaning extended from childbirth to succession, then to empress. In the modern form, the birthing figure would be 𠂆 and the child figure 𠮛.
According to Kōjien and 学研漢和大字典, ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 人 (“person (variant form)”) + 口 (“hole”) — a depiction of a person's (人) anus, with the additional meaning of “behind”, “rear”, as well as coming to mean “emperor/empress”, who would live in a palace “behind” worldly troubles.
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *mV-qow (“head”). Cognate with Tibetan གོ (go, “head; headman”), མགོ (mgo, “head, top, beginning”).
繼體君也。象人之形。施令以告四方，故厂之。从一、口。發號者，君后也。凡后之屬皆从后。
queen, empress, sovereign; (simp. for 後) behind, rear, after

Etymological analysis: pictographic
One step 彳 coming behind another 夂; 幺 provides the pronunciation
Phonosemantic compound. 幺 represents the sound, and 彳 (walk) and 夂 (foot) are used together to depict following behind someone.
遲也。从彳、幺、夊者，後也。

In oracle bone script, ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 幺 (“thread”) + 夊 (“foot”) – a foot bound by a rope, thus lagging behind. The component 彳 was added afterwards to emphasize this action.
Note that the simplified form 后 is also a traditional character on its own, with a different meaning.
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *hwak (“below”) (STEDT). Cognate with Tibetan འོག ('og, “below”), Burmese အောက် (auk, “under; below”) (from Proto-Lolo-Burmese *ʔok (“lower side; below”)).
遲也。从彳、幺、夊者，後也。
behind, rear, after; descendents
